## 321098: reflection, distribution, and digit-factorization routes
Define S(n,r)={m:0<=m<=n, binomial(n,m)=r mod16}, with r odd. The involution m -> n-m preserves the coefficient. If n is odd it has no fixed point. If n=2h>0 its only possible fixed point is h, but binomial(2h,h)=2 binomial(2h-1,h-1) is even, so h is not in S. Thus every a16,r(n) is even for n>0. For n=0 the only nonzero count is 1, which is not divisible by3. Zero counts satisfy both divisibilities. Consequently the first of the seven implications holds for every n. The same involution gives only one factor2; an additional orbit action would have to preserve the actual residue modulo16. Lucas describes which positions are odd (m binary-subordinate to n), but does not determine their odd residues modulo16. Toggling an allowed binary digit therefore is not proved residue-preserving.
